Evaluate the Yang et al. EPS kernel before support normalization.

Parameters
----------
dela : float or array_like
    Dimensionless linear-collapse barrier at the indicated epoch, extrapolated in the
    same growth convention.
s1 : float or array_like
    Dimensionless linear variance S=sigma**2 at the indicated host/subhalo/support mass.
    Active EPS terms require positive variance gaps.
s2 : float or array_like
    Dimensionless linear variance S=sigma**2 at the indicated host/subhalo/support mass.
    Active EPS terms require positive variance gaps.

Returns
-------
array_like
    delta_a/[sqrt(2*pi)*(s2-s1)**(3/2)], on positive variance support.

Notes
-----
The EPS accretion kernel and, where used, host-history scatter 0.12-0.15*log10(Ma/M0)
follow Yang et al., Eqs. (12)-(14), (21). Finite-gap normalization and zero-barrier
limits are numerical treatments of that kernel, not new empirical fits.

The CDM population combines EPS accretion, lognormal concentration scatter, the selected
tidal solver and the strict c_t survival cut. Named catalogues retain abundance,
concentration and survival as separate factors; changing a numerical solver does not by
itself recalibrate any fitted physical relation.

References
----------

.. [cite-yang] Yang et al. (2011), An Analytical Model for the Accretion of Dark Matter Subhalos, Eqs. (7)-(16), (21).
    https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.1757

    Active EPS terms require positive variance gaps.

    Active EPS terms require positive variance gaps.

Returns
-------
numpy.ndarray
    Conditional variance kernel divided by its finite-support integral, including the
    zero-barrier-gap limit.

Notes
-----
The EPS accretion kernel and, where used, host-history scatter 0.12-0.15*log10(Ma/M0)
follow Yang et al., Eqs. (12)-(14), (21). Finite-gap normalization and zero-barrier
limits are numerical treatments of that kernel, not new empirical fits.

definitions.doc_after:
Generate an ITAMAE weighted catalog while preserving SASHIMI physics.

Parameters
----------
M0 : float
    Reference host M200 in the variant internal mass unit. M0 normally refers to z=0;
    explicit epoch flags are described by the caller.
redshift : float
    Nonnegative target redshift of the subhalo population.
dz : float
    Positive nominal spacing of the accretion-redshift quadrature grid.
zmax : float
    Largest requested accretion redshift, above the target epoch; the actual grid
    convention belongs to this variant.
N_ma : int
    Number of logarithmically spaced accretion-mass nodes.
sigmalogc : float
    Nonnegative standard deviation of log10 concentration, in dex.
N_herm : int
    Positive Gauss-Hermite quadrature order for the scatter integrated by this routine:
    concentration in catalogue stages or host history in Na_calc.
logmamin : float, optional
    Lower or upper log10(M200_acc/Msun) bound. A None upper bound uses the model
    host-relative mass limit.
logmamax : float, optional
    Lower or upper log10(M200_acc/Msun) bound. A None upper bound uses the model
    host-relative mass limit.
N_hermNa : int
    Positive Gauss-Hermite order for the host-history scatter in the EPS accretion rate.
Na_model : {1, 2, 3}
    Yang EPS accretion/normalization prescription. This is a physical model selection,
    not a numerical tolerance.
ct_th : float
    Dimensionless tidal truncation threshold r_t/r_s; the specified strict survival rule
    is applied once through its mask.
profile_change : bool
    Apply the variant tidal response of scale radius and density in addition to
    bound-mass loss.
M0_at_redshift : bool
    Interpret the input host mass at the target redshift and invert the prescribed
    history to obtain its z=0 reference value.
method : str
    Explicit tidal integration method: picard_table, dop853, odeint or a retained
    perturbative approximation.
**kwargs : dict
    Additional keyword options forwarded to the called routine; reserved scientific
    controls remain owned by that routine.

Returns
-------
itamae.types.WeightedSubhaloCatalog
    Catalog with separate population, concentration, and survival
    weights. The product of population and concentration weights equals
    the historical tuple ``weight``; survival remains an independent
    factor for diagnostics and reweighting.

Notes
-----
The retained default scatter sigma(log10(c)) = 0.128 dex is the Ishiyama et al. Eq. (7),
Fig. 10 value for z=0 halos of 1e9 to 1e10 solar masses; Hiroshima et al. adopt the
rounded value 0.13 dex. Using one value across masses and redshifts is a model
assumption, not a quadrature error or a new calibration. The literature threshold rt/rs
> 0.77 follows the Hayashi et al. disruption prescription adopted by Hiroshima et al. A
caller-supplied threshold takes precedence in variants that expose it (C and SI
currently default to 0). This is a model selection rule; an exact-boundary test does not
calibrate disruption physics.

Catalogue masses and lengths are Msun and Mpc in this C implementation, densities
Msun/Mpc^3. All accretion nodes are retained; weight_final includes the survival mask.
The legacy tuple exposes the same nodes with a separate mask. The z grid uses the
retained arange(target+dz,zmax+dz,dz) convention, so a non-aligned zmax can be exceeded
by less than one nominal step.

References
----------

.. [cite-scatter] Ishiyama et al. (2013), The Cosmogrid Simulation: Statistical Properties of Small Dark Matter Halos, Eq. (7), Fig. 10.
    https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.2020

.. [cite-structure] Hiroshima, Ando & Ishiyama (2018), Modeling evolution of dark matter substructure and annihilation boost, Section II, Eqs. (4)-(9), (28), (34).
    https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.07691

.. [cite-survival] Hayashi et al. (2003), The Structural Evolution of Substructure, Section 2.1.
    https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0203004

Compute a CDM population and retain surviving nodes for the standard observable
reductions.

Parameters
----------
M0_per_Msun : float

N_hermNa : int
    Positive Gauss-Hermite order for the host-history scatter in the EPS accretion rate.
Na_model : {1, 2, 3}
    Yang EPS accretion/normalization prescription. This is a physical model selection,
    not a numerical tolerance.
ct_th : float
    Dimensionless tidal truncation threshold r_t/r_s; the specified strict survival rule
    is applied once through its mask.
profile_change : bool
    Apply the variant tidal response of scale radius and density in addition to
    bound-mass loss.
M0_at_redshift : bool
    Interpret the input host mass at the target redshift and invert the prescribed
    history to obtain its z=0 reference value.
prompt_cusps : bool
    Enable the variant prompt-cusp prescription and its explicitly supplied spectrum
    inputs.
k_fs_Mpc : float
    Free-streaming wavenumber numerical value in Mpc^-1 for the prompt-cusp spectrum
    prescription.
filter : str
    Named physical smoothing/filter prescription used in the prompt-cusp calculation.
alpha : float
    Dimensionless shape parameter of the selected prompt-cusp filter/transfer
    prescription.
method : str
    Explicit tidal integration method: picard_table, dop853, odeint or a retained
    perturbative approximation.
cosmology_backend : CosmologyBackend, optional
    ITAMAE background provider. The variant checks compatibility with the cosmology of
    its fitted halo relations.
data_dir : pathlib.Path or str, optional
    Explicit root of the required scientific input tables or generated products; no
    substitute spectrum is selected implicitly.
**kwargs : dict
    Additional keyword options forwarded to the called routine; reserved scientific
    controls remain owned by that routine.

Notes
-----
The NFW profile is from Navarro et al. The rounded factors rmax/rs = 2.163 (2.1626 where
explicitly used) and 4.625 are NFW maximum-circular-speed identities, as written in
Hiroshima et al., Eqs. (5)-(7), rather than independent empirical fits.

The retained default scatter sigma(log10(c)) = 0.128 dex is the Ishiyama et al. Eq. (7),
Fig. 10 value for z=0 halos of 1e9 to 1e10 solar masses; Hiroshima et al. adopt the
rounded value 0.13 dex. Using one value across masses and redshifts is a model
assumption, not a quadrature error or a new calibration. The literature threshold rt/rs

caller-supplied threshold takes precedence in variants that expose it (C and SI
currently default to 0). This is a model selection rule; an exact-boundary test does not
calibrate disruption physics.

If prompt cusps are enabled, the benchmark cutoff k_fs=1.06e6 Mpc**(-1) and sharp-k
multiplier alpha=1.8 follow the prompt-cusp model of Ando et al.; these are separate
from the CDM variance fit used by default.

The CDM population combines EPS accretion, lognormal concentration scatter, the selected
tidal solver and the strict c_t survival cut. Named catalogues retain abundance,
concentration and survival as separate factors; changing a numerical solver does not by
itself recalibrate any fitted physical relation.

definitions.doc_after:
Apply the historical SASHIMI-C truncation-concentration survival cut.

The strict ``c_t > ct_threshold`` comparison is the existing SASHIMI-C
catalog rule. Keeping it in the variant package makes the scientific
disruption prescription explicit while ITAMAE remains responsible only
for transporting and validating the resulting survival mask.

Parameters
----------
ct_threshold : float
    Dimensionless tidal truncation threshold r_t/r_s; the specified strict survival rule
    is applied once through its mask.

Notes
-----
The literature threshold rt/rs > 0.77 follows the Hayashi et al. disruption prescription
adopted by Hiroshima et al. A caller-supplied threshold takes precedence in variants

Returns

    Fraction of sampled peaks passing the epoch and shape collapse conditions.
J_cusp : numpy.ndarray
    Integral of rho**2 over physical volume for each collapsed cusp, in internal mass**2/length**3.

Notes
-----
The prompt-cusp prescription is Ando et al., Sections 2.1-2.3 and 3.1. Its sharp-k mapping
alpha=1.8 is a large-mass top-hat matching choice, explicitly not a direct microhalo-
simulation calibration.

Peak-height/curvature weighting and spectral moments use the BBKS Gaussian-peak
statistics; finite grids and Monte Carlo sizes are numerical choices.

The thermal benchmark and cusp/core prescription follow Delos & White; the luminosity
constant 0.531 follows Stucker et al. and Ando et al., Eq. (2.8). The retained
diagnostic fit with coefficient 0.08 is from Delos & White; it is evaluated internally
but is not returned by cusp_properties.

The cusp normalization is A=24*rho_dm0*a_coll**(-3/2)*R**(3/2), the outer radius is 0.11*a_coll*R, and the phase-space core uses the coefficient 3e-5. The luminosity uses 4*pi*A**2*[0.531+ln(rcusp/rcore)]. Internal population-average and 0.08 fit diagnostics are not return values. The historical implementation assumes a nonempty collapsed sample; its empty-sample path is not repaired by this documentation change.

Stucker et al. Eq. (14) gives the 0.531 luminosity approximation for r > 10*r_core.
The retained implementation evaluates it at r_cusp without enforcing that separation;
the citation does not validate results outside the stated large-radius regime.

planck.title: Planck Collaboration (2020), Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters, Table 2.
planck.manual_comparison: H0=67.36, Omega_m=0.3153, omega_b=0.02237, tau=0.0544 and A_s=2.100e-9 support the rounded native/control inputs. Omega_b is obtained by dividing omega_b by h^2. The Colossus planck18 preset selects a different data combination; its name does not make it identical to the native parameter vector.

growth.title: Carroll, Press & Turner (1992), The Cosmological Constant, Section 3.5.
growth.manual_comparison: The displayed growth suppression is g=2.5*Omega_m/[Omega_m^(4/7)-Omega_Lambda+(1+Omega_m/2)*(1+Omega_Lambda/70)]. The normalized D(z)=g(z)/[(1+z)*g(0)] and code redshift derivatives are derived uses. The DOI reaches a publisher landing page; the NED equation image provides accessible full text.

ludlow.title: Ludlow et al. (2016), The mass-concentration-redshift relation of cold and warm dark matter haloes, Appendix C.
ludlow.location: Eq. (3) and following text, p.5; Appendix C, pp.18-19, Eqs. (C8)-(C12)
ludlow.manual_comparison: The paper explicitly uses delta_sc(z)=1.686/D(z). The variance fit is sigma=22.26*xi^0.292/(1+1.53*xi^0.275+3.36*xi^0.198), xi=(M/(1e10 h^-1 Msun))^-1. It reports about 2.5% fit accuracy over 1e-7 to 1e15 h^-1 Msun. Differentiation is derived. WDM host histories integrate their spectrum and do not use this CDM variance fit; their redundant citation was removed.

correa.title: Correa et al. (2015), The accretion history of dark matter haloes - III. A physical model for the concentration-mass relation, Section 3 and Appendix B.
correa.location: Section 3, Eqs. (2)-(8), p.4; Appendix B, Eq. (B1), p.17
correa.manual_comparison: The anchored mass history, q=4.137*z_f^-0.9476 and z_f=-0.0064*log10(M)^2+0.0237*log10(M)+1.8837 are printed. Appendix B supplies both concentration-redshift branches and their coefficients. M is in physical Msun in these fits. History differentiation and combining a WDM spectrum with these coefficients are derived/adopted uses, not a WDM recalibration.

virial.title: Bryan & Norman (1998), Statistical Properties of X-ray Clusters: Analytic and Numerical Comparisons, Eq. (6).
virial.manual_comparison: For a flat matter-plus-Lambda cosmology the critical-density overdensity is 18*pi^2+82*x-39*x^2, x=Omega_m(z)-1. The paper reports roughly 1% fit accuracy for Omega_m(z)=0.1 to 1. This is distinct from a numerical solver tolerance and from an overdensity relative to mean matter.

conversion.title: Hu & Kravtsov (2003), Sample Variance Considerations for Cluster Surveys, Appendix C.
conversion.manual_comparison: The NFW mass-conversion approximation and inverse-fit coefficients are present. Eq. (C11) has a1=0.5116, a2=-0.4283, a3=-0.00313, a4=-3.52e-5, matching the code. The first value is 0.5116, not 1.5116. Root solving against the exact enclosed-mass identity is a separate derived conversion path.

nfw.title: Navarro, Frenk & White (1997), A Universal Density Profile from Hierarchical Clustering.
nfw.manual_comparison: The density and circular-speed laws are printed. f(x)=ln(1+x)-x/(1+x) follows by integrating the density. Potential with zero at infinity, exact mass-conversion root finding, and c=-1/W0(-exp[-(y+1)])-1 are derived consequences; the paper does not print the implementation's inverse or solver. The 2.163 and 4.625 factors are rounded maximum-speed identities.

tidal.title: Hiroshima, Ando & Ishiyama (2018), Modeling evolution of dark matter substructure and annihilation boost, Eqs. (23)-(24).
tidal.manual_comparison: Both CDM log10(A) and zeta mass/redshift coefficient lists match the displayed fits. The stated fit domain spans host masses 1e-6 to 1e16 Msun and redshifts 0 to 7. Reuse in other model backgrounds is an adopted prescription; solver agreement does not establish a new calibration.

structure.title: Hiroshima, Ando & Ishiyama (2018), Modeling evolution of dark matter substructure and annihilation boost, Section II, Eqs. (5)-(9).
structure.manual_comparison: The paper gives the concentration prescription, NFW speed/radius conversion and tidal structural response. Section II adopts scatter 0.13 dex; the disruption discussion and later selection factors use r_t/r_s=0.77. C/SI defaults allowing zero cutoff and all public 0.128-dex scatter defaults are explicit implementation choices, not literal copies of every population setting.

yang.title: Yang et al. (2011), An Analytical Model for the Accretion of Dark Matter Subhalos, Eqs. (12)-(14), (21).
yang.manual_comparison: The unnormalized EPS kernels, support normalization and sigma_log10(Ma)=0.12-0.15*log10(Ma/M0) are printed. Incomplete-gamma normalization and the continuous zero-gap limit are derived evaluations of Eqs. (8)-(9) and (12)-(14). WDM mass-dependent barriers and a fixed-gap normalization are a declared approximation; the low-redshift quantile continuation is not a new printed Yang equation.

parkinson.title: Parkinson, Cole & Helly (2008), Generating Dark Matter Halo Merger Trees, Section 3.1.
parkinson.manual_comparison: The multiplicative G power law and fitted parameters G0=0.57, gamma1=0.38, gamma2=-0.01 are present. They calibrate a merger-tree prescription to the Millennium reference used in that work; reuse in other variants does not recalibrate it.

tracks.title: Penarrubia et al. (2010), The impact of dark matter cusps and cores on the satellite galaxy population around spiral galaxies, Eq. (8), Fig. 6.
tracks.location: Eq. (8) and Fig. 6, p.8, gamma=1 row
tracks.manual_comparison: The response g(x)=2^mu*x^eta/(1+x)^mu has (mu,eta)=(0.4,0.3) for Vmax and (-0.3,0.4) for rmax in the gamma=1 row. Both displayed rows match the implementation. Applying this CDM tidal response before the SIDM correction or to a suppressed-power population is model composition.

survival.title: Hayashi et al. (2003), The Structural Evolution of Substructure.
survival.manual_comparison: The approximately 0.77*r_s bound concerns instantaneously truncated isotropic NFW systems. Adopting it as a subhalo survival selection follows the later Hiroshima prescription; it is not a universal empirical disruption threshold. Tests at the exact boundary establish mask and inversion behavior only.

scatter.title: Ishiyama et al. (2013), The Cosmogrid Simulation: Statistical Properties of Small Dark Matter Halos, Eq. (7), Fig. 10.
scatter.location: Eq. (7), Fig. 10 and accompanying text, p.10
scatter.manual_comparison: The reported width is 0.128 dex for c_vmax at z=0 and masses 1e9 to 1e10 Msun; the two other bins give 0.124 and 0.125. For an NFW profile c=2.163*c_vmax preserves logarithmic width. All directly exposed defaults inspected here are 0.128, consistent with their existing docs; Hiroshima rounds to 0.13. Extending a constant width across mass/redshift is an assumption.

prompt.title: Ando, Moro-Gonzalez & Li (2026), Prompt cusps in hierarchical dark matter halos: Implications for annihilation boost, Sections 2.1-2.3.
prompt.manual_comparison: The cusp normalization 24, outer radius 0.11, core coefficient 3e-5, luminosity 0.531, growth exponent 0.901, shape condition and collapse scale factor are present. The sharp-k alpha=1.8 choice occurs in Section 3.1, not Sections 2.1-2.3. The 100-GeV/30-MeV benchmark and cutoff are stated; the exact retained a_kd=5.3e-12 was not recovered from the cited text.

delos.title: Delos & White (2023), Prompt cusps and the dark matter annihilation signal.
delos.manual_comparison: The thermal cusp/core prescription, the 0.08 diagnostic fit and Gaussian-peak/ellipsoidal-collapse ingredients are present. Appendix A contains the growth exponent, collapse relation and peak distribution. Finite sampling grids and cached draws are implementation choices. The exact stored kinetic-decoupling scale factor remains without a verified literal source.

stucker.title: Stucker et al. (2023), The effect of stellar encounters on the dark matter annihilation signal from prompt cusps.
stucker.location: Eq. (14) and following domain statement, p.5
stucker.manual_comparison: J(<r)=4*pi*A^2*[0.531+ln(r/r_core)] is printed for r>10*r_core. The code evaluates it at r_cusp without an explicit domain check. The constant is supported, but the citation does not justify applying this large-radius approximation for arbitrary core-to-cusp radius ratios.

bbks.title: Bardeen, Bond, Kaiser & Szalay (1986), The Statistics of Peaks of Gaussian Random Fields, Appendix A.
bbks.location: Appendix A, Eqs. (A14)-(A15), PDF p.38 / printed p.52
bbks.manual_comparison: The joint peak-height/curvature density and f(x) error-function/exponential expression match the implementation. Delos & White Appendix A also reproduces them. Monte Carlo grids and numerical inversion are not part of the BBKS formula. The DOI redirect returned HTTP 405; the original ADS journal scan returned 200.

ellipsoid.title: Sheth, Mo & Tormen (2001), Ellipsoidal collapse and an improved model for the number and spatial distribution of dark matter haloes, Eq. (3), Appendix A.
ellipsoid.location: Eq. (3), p.3; Appendix A, Eq. (A3), p.12
ellipsoid.manual_comparison: The collapse relation uses beta=0.47 and gamma=0.615 with the sign rule equivalent to e^2-p*abs(p). Appendix A gives the conditional ellipticity/prolateness density. Changing variables to u=p/e and constructing an inversion sampler are derived numerical operations, not an algorithm printed in the paper.
